## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ekuttarikanaya* ("The numerical method") constitutes the seventh chapter of the *Parivāra*, the final collection of the Pali *Vinaya Piṭaka*. The text systematically organizes disciplinary and monastic rules and topics into numerical groupings ranging from one to eleven items, adopting a format analogous to the numerical taxonomy of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya*. An English translation of the work has been completed by Bhikkhu Brahmali. No independent discussions of the text appear in the secondary reference literature provided in the dossier.

 DharmaNexus strongly supports these alignments, finding extensive Pali-internal text reuse, with its largest concentrations in the *Upālipañcaka* (over 1,100 matches) and *Kammakkhandhaka* (over 900 matches), alongside extensive shared segments across the *Mahākhandhaka* (*Kd* 1) and multiple *nipātas* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (particularly AN 5, AN 7, AN 8, and AN 10), as well as the *Parivāra-aṭṭhakathā* and later Vinaya treatises [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali literature, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of the text with Sanskrit Vinaya sections (including the *Pravāraṇāvastu*, *Śayanāsanavastu*, and *Kośāmbakavastu*) and Tibetan Vinaya collections (the *Vinayavastu* and *Vinaya-kṣudraka-vastu*), as well as the Sanskrit *Daśabalasūtra* [DharmaNexus].
